summary: drafted six units for the four issue-3 proposals: two new nodes (backfill workflow, resume) plus additive revisions to spec-gate, spec-producer, conductor and workflows

detail: round 1 blocked on five findings. The load-bearing one: the corroboration stage's applicability was file-granular while its scope was diff-granular, so the stage would have blocked its own CR and the first CR to touch any of 37 corpus nodes carrying no extensions field. Re-derived to hunk granularity across all three artifact-read tells. The step-record tell was a fourth list keyed to a bar that did not exist and checking entry count rather than correspondence; re-derived as a correspondence check against the drawn graph, the map and the use cases, bound to a declarable bar. A generic per-step decision node was drawn for a rule with one real instance, making the (path class, edge) pair ill-defined for two scenarios; cut it and drew step 3's real three-way branch instead. One extensions row claimed a divergence the graph could not take; dropped as a co-owned seam owned by remediation-governance. The resume node asserted a per-segment attribution its own prose said did not exist; re-derived to the observable case, a smaller inherited set.

round 2 found two regressions against artifacts round 1's remediation changed. The severe one is self-inflicted: the edit that redrew the backfill CFG matched its section heading where the string also occurs inside the steps table, truncating the node from that point and destroying its Use Cases, Control Flow and Scenario map. The node's own rule then applies to its repair - rewrite whole from the CFG, not patch. The second: narrowing the tell's applicability from file to row did not stop the stage blocking its own CR, because this CR edits a use-case row in a node that states no extensions anywhere.

why.blast: medium - the SDD self-spec's authoring and gate nodes
why.novelty: medium - two design forks the judge ruled a third remediation round cannot settle by editing
why.confidence: low - two of round 2's four findings are regressions against round 1's own remediation, so the loop is not converging and the doctrine stops it for a re-plan

detail: post-re-plan round: oracle and builder passed, architect failed on two. The load-bearing one is that the rewritten backfill graph routed every re-derivation through step one unconditionally, which encodes re-run-from-the-top - the exact behavior the node exists to forbid, and stated twice in its own prose. Redrawn as a decision over the earliest implicated step with both arms mapped, and a negative scenario added asserting steps before the re-entry point keep their entries. Also removed a dangling bar identifier for a governance that does not exist (the tell fires on the relayed mode, so it needs no registry entry), corrected a measured count that was off by one inside the rationale of a stage whose thesis is check-the-artifact-not-the-claim, and named two residual escapes rather than leaving them implied. Provenance: these are findings against content this round's re-plan authored, not against a prior remediation round's fix; the loop is converging - oracle and builder went FAIL, FAIL, PASS and the architect findings narrowed from the stage blocking its own CR to one graph edge and one name.
